caption: FIGURE 5: MetaOpt automatically converts the bi-level problem to a single-level optimization. It supports any follower, which either (1) is a convex optimization; (2) is a feasibility problem; or (3) has an objective that aligns with the outer problem.
subject: how MetaOpt decides whether to leave an inner problem as is, mark it NA, or rewrite it via primal-dual KKT

groups.why_chosen: MetaOpt avoids needlessly rewriting an inner problem: if aligned with the outer objective or merely a feasibility problem, its constraints are merged in as is; otherwise a convex problem gets a primal-dual/KKT rewrite, and anything else is marked NA.
groups.what_to_learn: A left-to-right diamond cascade: `Y` drops to a terminal box, `N` continues right, so the unhandled case lands last
